so I have been going back and forth on how the cache should work and I think I finally have it straight in my head, the thing is that right now every single request goes out to the index and that is fine when the index is small but the moment it grows past a few hundred thousand rows the latency is just not acceptable anymore, and people notice, they really notice, they start complaining that search feels slow even when the results are good. So what I want to do is put a layer in front of it, and originally I thought we should cache the rendered results, no wait, that is wrong, we should cache the query plan and not the rendered results, because the rendered results go stale the moment anyone edits a document and then we are serving wrong data which is worse than being slow. The query plan is stable for much longer. And here is the part that actually matters, if we cache the plan then we get better tail latency, and better tail latency is what people actually perceive as the product being fast, not the median, the median is already fine. Nobody has ever complained about the median. They complain about the one request in fifty that takes two seconds. So the win is not average speed at all, it is consistency. We could expand this later to the suggestion endpoint too, and maybe the typeahead, although typeahead has its own problems because it fires on every keystroke and I do not think a plan cache helps there, that probably needs debouncing instead. Anyway I think this is getting a bit broad, let me pull it back. The concrete thing I want is a plan cache in front of the index, keyed on the normalised query, with a short time to live so that a schema change cannot poison it for long. That is the whole proposal really.
